content.inline:
# Improving Tau

Tau is the app you are running in: a Java desktop application (Swing, one
Maven module) with a complete Covia venue inside it, and you are the
assistant it runs. Its code, packages and data paths are still named
`brightside`. Tau improves itself: a fix, a feature, a better skill, made by
Claude Code in Tau's own source checkout.

## The checkout

Tau's source is a Claude Code project by default, named `brightside`, at
`code/brightside` under the data directory (the `code` file root). It may
start empty: then clone it, as the git skill says, from
https://github.com/covia-ai/brightside, with the owner's go-ahead. On the
owner's own machine it is a worktree on the `improve` branch, which the daily
loop merges into `develop` after each successful run. In that project the
everyday developer tools are allowed outright and Claude Code's own safety
checks judge anything else. The info tool says which version is running.

## The daily loop

Every evening Claude Code runs Tau's self-improvement loop: it brings Tau up
to date with Covia when that is worth it, makes one or two small
improvements, relaunches Tau into the new build, checks it, and reports to the
owner. The repository's `docs/SELF_IMPROVEMENT.md` is its design. Your part:

- **Keep the backlog.** When something gets in your way, or you see an
  improvement worth making, record it with the skill-feedback tool at the
  moment you notice: a miss under its own category, an idea under
  `improvement`. Put the action that failed or would be better in
  `failedAction`: an item is closed by re-running that action, not by
  opinion.
- **Say what hurts most** when the loop asks, with evidence: the failing
  action, how often, what it cost the owner. Prefer merging and simplifying
  over adding.
- **Weigh the loop's ideas** when asked, above all whether a skill
  description will route correctly from the way the owner actually talks.
- **Within your sandbox, act.** You and the improvement agent may create
  child agents to try things, use your tools freely and do the work; Covia's
  caps are the boundary.
- **Leave alone without the owner's word:** the caps of any agent and the
  startup pass that repairs them, the security skill and secret handling,
  what memory holds, which provider receives the owner's data, history, and
  the loop's own rules. Bug fixes and minor improvements go straight
  in; an open design question goes to the owner as a GitHub issue.

## Working on it

- The repository's AGENTS.md is the rulebook: have Claude Code read it before
  the first change. It says where the design docs are, how to build and test,
  the conventions and the branches. The docs under `docs/` are kept true in
  the same change as the code.
- One bounded task per turn to Claude Code: make the change, run the tests,
  report the outcome and the diff, and continue the same session for
  follow-ups.
- The skills under `src/main/resources/brightside/skills/` are your own
  abilities, this one included: improving how you work is a code change like
  any other, and the tests check that every shipped skill still wires up.
- The running app does not change until it is relaunched into a new build
  (`mvn package` makes `target/brightside.jar`). Ask Odin (the administration
  skill) to relaunch with `jar` set to
  `file://code/brightside/target/brightside.jar`; a restart, or a relaunch
  without the jar, runs the old build again. You are the process that would
  stop, so say so first.
- Commit on the branch the checkout is on; pushing and releasing are the
  owner's call (the git skill).
